title: Prime quotient of a normalization over a Japanese base quotient is finite
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $T\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $P\subset T$ be a prime ideal and put $p=P\cap R$, the inverse image under $R\to T$. If the domain $R/p$ is Japanese (N-2) [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], then $T/P$ is a finitely generated $R/p$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] for the injective map $R/p\to T/P$ induced by $R\to T$. No Noetherianity of $T$, normality of $R$, separability of $L/K$, or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Marot, Sur les anneaux universellement japonais, Bulletin de la SMF 103 (1975), Lemma 1.1, printed p.104; standing hypotheses immediately above the lemma. DOI 10.24033/bsmf.1795. Read online; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=R/p$ and $B=T/P$. The map $A\to B$ is injective: a class $r+p$ maps to zero exactly when $r\in P\cap R=p$. Since $P$ is prime, $B$ is a domain, and its subring $A$ is a domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] to the quotient map $R\twoheadrightarrow A$ to see that $A$ is Noetherian. Write $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$; the injection extends to $k\hookrightarrow E$ by $a/b\mapsto a/b$, since nonzero denominators stay nonzero.

source.place: Marot (1975), Lemma 1.1 and standing hypotheses, printed p.104 (PDF p.3). Read online; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-almost-finite-residue-field-degree] with its $F=L$, $C=T$, $Q=P$. Its base $R$ is a Noetherian domain and $L/K$ is finite by hypothesis. Every element of $T$ is integral over $R$ because $T$ is the integral closure. The lemma gives $[E:k]<\infty$, without assuming that $T$ is Noetherian or finite over $R$.

source.place: Marot (1975), Lemma 1.1 and standing hypotheses, printed p.104 (PDF p.3). Read online; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $D$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $E$. For $t\in T$, choose a monic relation $t^n+r_{n-1}t^{n-1}+\cdots+r_0=0$ with $r_i\in R$. Reducing modulo $P$ gives $(t+P)^n+(r_{n-1}+p)(t+P)^{n-1}+\cdots+(r_0+p)=0$. Thus each element of $B$ lies in $D$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and $B$ is an $A$-submodule of $D$. Since $A$ is Japanese and $E/k$ is finite, the definition [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] says exactly that $D$ is a finitely generated $A$-module.

source.place: Marot (1975), Lemma 1.1 and standing hypotheses, printed p.104 (PDF p.3). Read online; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to the Noetherian ring $A$, its finite module $D$, and the $A$-submodule $B\subseteq D$. It follows that $B=T/P$ is a finitely generated $A=R/p$-module for the injection of Step 1, as required.
